draft.title: Hypothetical RAG Sanity Check: Comparing Retrieval On vs. Off for Local LLMs
draft.body: This post outlines a hypothetical experiment for sanity-checking Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) setups with local LLMs. The scenario involves using 30 local documents as a knowledge base. The core idea is to compare model responses under two distinct conditions: retrieval enabled and retrieval disabled, using the exact same set of questions. This direct comparison aims to highlight the impact of the retrieval component on answer generation. It's important to note that this is a hypothetical experiment, and no actual accuracy results or benchmarks are available. The methodology should accommodate questions that may not have answers within the provided documents, allowing for observation of how the RAG system (or the base LLM without retrieval) handles such cases. The goal is to provide a framework for evaluating RAG effectiveness without relying on pre-existing performance data.

draft.title: Designing a Hypothetical RAG Evaluation for Local LLMs: Retrieval On vs. Off
draft.body: We propose a hypothetical framework for evaluating the sanity of a RAG system operating with local LLMs. The setup is designed around a corpus of 30 local documents. The central tenet of this hypothetical evaluation is a direct comparison: posing the same questions to the LLM with RAG retrieval enabled, and then with retrieval explicitly turned off. This contrast is intended to isolate and demonstrate the contribution of the retrieval mechanism. Crucially, this remains a hypothetical exercise; no real-world measurements or accuracy figures are generated or presented. The proposed method must also account for questions that lack corresponding answers within the 30 documents, observing how both configurations (retrieval on/off) respond to such queries. The objective is to conceptualize a basic RAG validation process, emphasizing the comparison of retrieval's influence on output quality.
draft.plan: Describe a hypothetical RAG evaluation design. Use 30 local documents as the knowledge base. Emphasize the comparison between retrieval-enabled and retrieval-disabled modes for the same queries. Include the scenario of questions without answers in the documents. Reiterate the hypothetical status and absence of measured outcomes.
